 Summary
 Yoo Yeon-seok and Seo Hyun-jin reunite on screen 10 years after Dr. Romantic, shifting from medical colleagues who shared life-and-death bonds to opposing legal rivals on opposite sides of a courtroom.
 Centered on "two conflicting memories of the same night," the plot bypasses conventional whodunit tropes to confront human blind spots and trial by public opinion in East Asian society.
 Remade from the acclaimed British ITV thriller series Liar and directed by Cho Young-min, the drama unfolds across three distinct chapters packed with fast-paced twists.
 The series premieres on October 30, 2026, airing Fridays and Saturdays on South Korea's MBC, while viewers in Taiwan and Hong Kong can stream it on Disney+.
 A decade ago in Romantic Doctor, Teacher Kim, the chemistry between Kang Dong-joo and Yoon Seo-jung working side by side at Doldam Hospital became an unforgettable classic for K-drama fans. Ten years later, Yoo Yeon-seok and Seo Hyun-jin finally reunite on the small screen. But viewers expecting a romantic sequel should take a deep breath first: in MBC’s new thriller series The Perfect Lie, the pair set romance aside for a high-stakes psychological battle over conflicting memories.
 Read more : Moving into each other’s homes before even meeting? New Korean dating show Swap Life pieces together sparks through three days of living traces 
 A seemingly perfect date turns into a Rashomon-style mystery by morning
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by MBC DRAMA official (@mbcdrama_now) 
 Adapted from the acclaimed British ITV thriller Liar, The Perfect Lie begins simply enough: Yoo Yeon-seok plays cardiac surgeon Min Jun-ho, a single father raising his son after his wife’s passing, known for his warm personality and deeply respected at work. Seo Hyun-jin plays schoolteacher Kang Ji-sun, who built up an emotional shield after childhood hardships but finds herself moved by Jun-ho’s sincerity. 
 Set up by mutual friends, their first date goes wonderfully. Yet come morning, the romance shatters. Ji-sun walks into a police station claiming she was assaulted the night before, while Jun-ho looks entirely bewildered during questioning, convinced their night together was completely mutual. One night, two completely different stories. Who is lying, and who selectively altered their memories? Right out of the gate, the show throws a brutal test of trust at the audience. 
 From saving lives together to courtroom confrontation: a masterclass acting duel ten years in the making
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by MBC DRAMA official (@mbcdrama_now) 
 The two had some intriguing thoughts to share at the press conference about teaming up again. Seo Hyun-jin laughed that because they know each other’s acting rhythm so well, they needed zero adjustment period on the very first day of filming, feeling as natural as if they’d been working together for months. Yoo Yeon-seok added that compared to ten years ago, Seo Hyun-jin brings even more ease and softness to her performance, making it immensely reassuring to work with her again. 
 Yet that off-screen familiarity turns into the most dangerous chemistry on camera. In the show, Min Jun-ho’s smile is impossibly gentle, which is precisely why it sends chills down your spine trying to figure out if his warmth is genuine. Seo Hyun-jin delivers a spot-on performance capturing the rage, self-blame, and confusion following trauma, her eyes filled with guard and the shock of betrayal. As these two powerhouse actors drop their medical gowns to square off in an interrogation room, every micro-expression becomes a clue for the audience trying to spot the lie. 
 Beyond finding the truth: holding a mirror to societal judgment in East Asia
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by MBC DRAMA official (@mbcdrama_now) 
 Adapting Western thrillers is always a test of local integration. Directed by Cho Young-min (Do You Like Brahms?, The Interest of Love), The Perfect Lie features a restrained yet tense visual style. While keeping the intricate structure of the original, the Korean adaptation digs into pressing issues unique to East Asian society: the social expectations weighed on a single father, the victim-blaming a female teacher faces after a sexual assault, and how truth gets twisted and consumed in the court of online public opinion.
 The drama unfolds across three core chapters. It doesn’t simply ask viewers to guess “who the bad guy is.” Instead, as the lives of both protagonists crumble, it asks a deeper question: why do people so often choose to believe only the lies they want to believe?
 The Perfect Lie premiered on October 30, 2026, airing every Friday and Saturday on South Korea’s MBC, and is available for international audiences to stream on Disney+. If you want to see Yoo Yeon-seok and Seo Hyun-jin tear through the illusion of trust with top-tier acting, make sure to add this one to your watchlist.
